business_problem: Japan Airlines needed to modernize finance systems built on SAP ECC, SAP EC-CS, and Business Warehouse before end-of-service deadlines while improving agility, reducing paper-based processes, and continuing a major transformation program despite pandemic disruption.
solution_summary: Japan Airlines worked with IBM Consulting to rebuild its eJAL finance platform around SAP S/4HANA and a cloud-first architecture that fit the airline’s broader hybrid strategy. IBM helped redesign workflows around ESG and operational reporting requirements, migrate core finance processes off SAP ECC and SAP EC-CS, and deploy the new environment on SAP HANA Enterprise Cloud with AWS so it could interoperate with JAL’s internal CIEL/S hybrid cloud platform. IBM also guided the selection of SAP Analysis for Microsoft Office and SAP Analytics Cloud to replace spreadsheet-heavy reporting with shared visibility into cash flow, costs, and shared assets. The program was executed through a fully remote delivery model during COVID restrictions, giving JAL a more elastic, disaster-resilient platform and faster access to near-real-time analytics for planning and per-flight cost decisions.

data_flow: Financial and accounting processes move from legacy SAP ECC and EC-CS applications into SAP S/4HANA on SAP HANA Enterprise Cloud with AWS; reporting data then feeds SAP Analysis for Microsoft Office and SAP Analytics Cloud so finance teams can analyze cash flow, costs, assets, and per-flight performance with far less manual spreadsheet work.
business_outcome: JAL completed the migration on schedule through a 100% remote rollout, cut customizations dramatically, reduced SAP add-ons from 1,260 to 500, lowered maintenance burden, and gained faster, more reliable finance reporting and analytics for operational decisions.
